item.title: AES Exhibition 2024 date announced
item.description: The AES is delighted to announce that the society will hold its annual exhibition and trade fair on 28th September 2024. Once again the event will be held at Kempton Park Racecourse, Sunbury-on-Thames, TW16 5AQ. This flagship event will be the harbinger of our 90th anniversary year as an entomological society, in 2025. item.title: Remembering Duncan Fraser
item.description: We were saddened to learn of the passing of Duncan Fraser, a retired veterinary surgeon of Capel, Surrey. Duncan was awarded our Cribb award for outstanding contributions to conservation, in 2005, for his work at Old Stores Meadows private nature reserve, 15 acres of agricultural land which he returned to nature, with great success. Information about the project is available on YouTube, here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uB4jkL04DzE

item.title: Riverfly Handbook published
item.description: Hot off the press: Craig Macadam's book on the Riverflies of the UK. This new publication will help you study the Riverflies (mayflies, stoneflies and caddisflies). Authored by Craig R. Macadam with contributions from Dr Ian Wallace the Riverfly Handbook covers where to find them, how to study them and identify them. item.title: Colin Plant awarded the Marsh Award for Entomology
item.description: Our congratulations go to Colin Plant, who has been awarded the Marsh Award for Entomology. The award was for Colin's numerous entomological endeavours over many years, including editing our journal, the Entomologist's Record. Colin took over that editorial role in 1995 - almost 30 years ago - taking over from Paul Sokoloff. It was Colin who brought the journal into the AES fold, thereby safeguarding its financial fortunes.

item.title: Nick Baker to become Patron of the AES
item.description: We are delighted to announce that the naturalist and broadcaster Nick Baker has agreed to become the first-ever Patron of the AES, on the 90th anniversary of the Society. Nick is well known for his work with the BBC, which has included TV programmes such as The Really Wild Show, Autumnwatch and Springwatch Unsprung. item.title: End of an Era: Invertebrate Conservation News Ceases Publication
item.description: After more than 50 years of publication, Invertebrate Conservation News (ICN) is coming to a close. Following the sad passing of long-time editor David Lonsdale in April 2024, we've been unable to find someone to take on the role, so the decision has been made to stop publishing the newsletter. PDF back issues are still available for AES members in the members' area of our website, and older editions can be found on the Biodiversity Heritage Library.
